extracted.intended_audience: general readers; aspiring public officers, tradesmen, and those seeking practical moral/household advice (18th-century readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and prescriptive rules for conduct in public office, private life, health, sleep, commerce, and study — the kind of practical-moral advice essays Benjamin Franklin produces for a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess state's expenses and revenue before reform
rubrics_metrics.description: “Tell me, at least, the expenses of the republic, for no doubt you intend to retrench the superfluous?” / “I never thought of this either.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to ‘enrich the republic’ or retrench spending until you know both its expenses and revenue. Practical governance requires written accounts and concrete knowledge of finances before proposing reforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know relative military strength before undertaking war
rubrics_metrics.description: Before undertaking a war one 'ought to know the strength on both sides' so that if one's party is stronger one may advise war, and if weaker one may dissuade the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure forces by sea and land; obtain lists in writing; avoid rash decisions based on ambition rather than a sober appraisal of capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect and verify garrisons before disbanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not remove garrisons on mere suspicion they 'ruin a country on pretence of defending it' without having seen how they behave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal inspection and evidence are required before proposing to reinforce or disband garrisons; advice based on conjecture should be withheld until verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine mines, production, and provisions before policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You have never been at the mines of silver ... I believe you have at least observed how much corn our land produces, how long it will serve to supply our city, and how much more we shall want for the whole year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy decisions must rest on empirical checks: visit resource sites, measure agricultural output, and estimate provisions to avoid scarcity and make timely orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove competence in private affairs before public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Why did you not first try to retrieve your uncle's affairs ... after having given that proof of your industry, you might have taken a greater trust upon you.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable success managing private responsibilities is the reasonable test for suitability to govern larger public duties; avoid accepting public office when you cannot manage smaller obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disorderly ambition; speak only on what you understand
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Take heed lest too great a desire of power should render you despised; consider how dangerous it is to speak ... concerning things we do not understand.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation and honour come from understanding and competence; rashness and pretence attract blame and contempt. Counsel self-knowledge and humility before public action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflect on consumption and reform wasted life
rubrics_metrics.description: Anergus computes what he has consumed in ten years and cries, 'What have I done all this time for God or man? ... Oh shameful waste of life and time!' leading him to reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic accounting of one’s use of time and resources can motivate conversion from idle, wasteful living to a life of useful knowledge and public service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue is not identical with self-denial
rubrics_metrics.description: It is commonly asserted that without self-denial there is no virtue ... If self-denial be the essence of virtue, then ... the man who is naturally temperate, just, etc., is not virtuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish virtue (temperance, justice, etc.) from mere self-denial: virtues are real whether practised against temptation or through natural inclination. 'Merit' (desert) may be greater where actions resist temptation, but natural virtue is still virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-denial counts as merit only when resisting vice
rubrics_metrics.description: The self-denial here meant must be when our inclinations are towards vice ... By merit is understood desert; when a man merits, we mean that he deserves praise or reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating merit, consider whether someone acted against a contrary inclination; denying a vicious inclination exhibits merit relative to those who are naturally virtuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic is essential to commerce and everyday business
rubrics_metrics.description: No business, commerce, trade, or employment whatsoever ... can be managed and carried on without the assistance of numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Traders, shopkeepers, and people in nearly every calling require arithmetic to compute values, profit and loss, and to know their financial position at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry underpins arts, mechanics, navigation, and surveying
rubrics_metrics.description: No curious art or mechanic work can either be invented, improved, or performed without [geometry's] assisting principles ... architects, mariners, engineers, surveyors, gaugers use geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometry is practically indispensable for architecture, ship navigation, fortifications, surveying land, measuring capacities and areas, and for astronomical and geographical work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical demonstrations train the mind for exact reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical demonstrations ... serving to a just formation of the mind, enlarging its capacity, and strengthening it so as to render the same capable of exact reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studying mathematics improves reasoning and the ability to discern truth from falsehood across subjects; it is useful even to those for whom the specific techniques are not directly applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve health by exercise and temperance to ensure pleasant dreams
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to be careful in preserving health, by due exercise and great temperance; for in sickness the imagination is disturbed, and disagreeable ... ideas are apt to present themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular exercise (preceding meals) and moderate eating promote good digestion and undisturbed sleep, reducing nightmares and unpleasant dreams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise before meals; avoid heavy suppers after full dinners
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise should precede meals ... If, after exercise, we feed sparingly, the digestion will be easy ... Supers are not bad if we have not dined; but restless nights naturally follow hearty suppers after full dinners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match food intake to activity: those who move more may eat more; avoid heavy late suppers after a full dinner to prevent disturbed sleep or dangerous consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a constant supply of fresh air in the bedchamber
rubrics_metrics.description: Another means of preserving health ... is the having a constant supply of fresh air in your bedchamber. It has been a great mistake, the sleeping in rooms exactly closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sleeping in tightly closed rooms or behind curtains; fresh air prevents accumulation of 'perspirable matter' that causes uneasiness and bad dreams. Airing bedrooms and avoiding overcrowding is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use porous/thinner bedclothes and ventilate bedding when awakened
rubrics_metrics.description: By using thinner and more porous bedclothes, which will suffer the perspirable matter more easily to pass through them ... get out of bed, beat up and turn your pillow, shake the bedclothes well ... leave it to cool; walk about till your skin has had time to discharge its load.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical remedies for waking in a hot bed: ventilate bedding, change or shift to a cool bed, walk undressed to allow skin to discharge moisture, or at least lift bedding repeatedly to draw in fresh air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange pillow and limbs to avoid pressure that disturbs sleep
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be taken, when you lie down, to dispose your pillow so as to suit your manner of placing your head ... then place your limbs so as not to bear inconveniently hard upon one another ... the uneasiness may come on while you are asleep, and disturb your imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comfortable, pressure-free sleeping posture prevents localized pain from developing during sleep and producing disturbing dreams.

rubrics_metrics.name: A good conscience is fundamental to pleasant dreams
rubrics_metrics.description: But, though they will generally prove effectual in producing the end intended, there is a case ... when the person ... has not taken care to preserve, what is necessary above all things, A GOOD CONSCIENCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral tranquillity and a clear conscience are presented as the ultimate condition for pleasant dreams; physical measures help, but conscience is decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time is money
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that time is money. He that can earn ten shillings a day ... and goes abroad or sits idle one half of that day ... has really spent, or, rather, thrown away, five shillings besides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat idle time as a real economic loss measured by foregone earnings; guard against trivial diversions that consume productive hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit is money; keep accounts and guard credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that credit is money. If a man lets his money lie in my hands after it is due, he gives me the interest ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain punctual payments and be mindful that reputation for prompt payment enables borrowing and business opportunities; keep exact accounts to discover small leakages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money begets money — compound gains from reinvestment
rubrics_metrics.description: Remember that money is of the prolific, generating nature. Money can beget money, and its offspring can beget more, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest returns to compound gains; small sums turned repeatedly grow substantially over time—avoid destroying future generations of returns by wasteful consumption (analogy: killing a breeding sow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctual paymasterhood secures others' purse and credit
rubrics_metrics.description: The good paymaster is lord of another man's purse ... He that is known to pay punctually ... may at any time ... raise all the money his friends can spare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuality in payment builds trust and access to credit; never keep borrowed money beyond promised time lest lenders withdraw support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appear industrious to preserve creditor confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The sound of your hammer at five in the morning ... makes him easy six months longer; but if he sees you at a billiard-table ... he sends for his money the next day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small visible signals of diligence materially affect a creditor's willingness to extend credit. Guard public behaviours that influence perceptions of reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep exact accounts to detect trifling expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent this, keep an exact account for some time both of your expenses and your income ... you will discover how wonderfully small, trifling expenses mount up to large sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording particulars reveals small habitual expenses that accumulate; use bookkeeping to correct wasteful habits and align living with true means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry and frugality are the way to wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: In short, the way to wealth ... depends chiefly on two words, industry and frugality; that is, waste neither time nor money, but make the best use of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire honestly, save what you can (necessary expenses excepted), and combine industrious work with frugal habits to amass wealth over time, subject to providential contingencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eat and drink in quantities suited to constitution and occupation
rubrics_metrics.description: Eat and drink such an exact quantity as the constitution of thy body allows of, in reference to the services of the mind. They that study much ought not to eat so much as those that work hard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust food intake to bodily constitution, age, occupation, and temperament; the proper quantity enables good digestion and nourishment without excess.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excess in all things; eat for necessity not pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess in all other things whatever, as well as in meat and drink, is also to be avoided ... Eat for necessity, not pleasure; for lust knows not where necessity ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-discipline in consumption promotes long life, health, and vigour of mind; cultivate appetite reasoned by necessity rather than indulgence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure food proportionally to stomach's capacity and constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The measure of food ought to be (as much as possibly may be) exactly proportionable to the quality and condition of the stomach, because the stomach digests it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose both quantity and quality of food appropriate to digestive capacity; some foods allow greater quantity due to lighter digestion. Tailor diet by complexion (phlegmatic, choleric), age, and health.
